c.tagline: Japan's steaming onsen capital, where the earth itself boils over.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis have automatic rear doors and are metered; fares run higher late at night, and having your destination written in Japanese helps since drivers rarely speak English.

emergency.note: 110 for police, 119 for ambulance/fire; a multilingual tourist support hotline is also available.

hood_desc: The most famous onsen district, built directly around the sulfurous steam vents of the 'Jigoku' (hells), a cluster of surreal, colorfully mineral-stained hot springs open for viewing. Steam rises from drains and vents throughout the neighborhood, and jigoku-mushi steam-cooked food stalls are everywhere.

The commercial heart of the city around Beppu Station, with the retro public bathhouse Takegawara Onsen, shopping arcades, and easy access to trains and buses. It's the most convenient base for first-time visitors.

A hillside hot-spring hamlet famous for its thatched-roof yunohana steam huts, where mineral crystals are harvested from the steam for bath salts. The sulfur smell and misty hillside views give it a distinctly otherworldly atmosphere.

A quieter, more local onsen town north of central Beppu, known for Shibaseki Onsen, a rustic bathhouse built right into the tidal rocks on the beach. It's popular with residents rather than tour groups.

A residential onsen neighborhood in the hills above the city, home to Hyotan Onsen, a beloved public bathhouse with an outdoor gourd-shaped pool, waterfall bath, and sand bath. It offers sweeping views over Beppu Bay.

water.note: Tap water is safe and pleasant to drink.

transit.hours: Kamenoi Bus runs roughly 6:00-22:00; JR trains keep similar hours
transit.note: Kamenoi Bus's Jigoku Meguri loop line links Beppu Station to the Kannawa hot-spring hell district.

train: JR Nippo Main Line; limited express 'Sonic' service to Fukuoka/Kokura and local trains to Oita
bus: Highway buses to Fukuoka, Kumamoto, and Oita
ferry: Overnight Sunflower ferry service to Osaka/Kobe

airport.name: Oita Airport (OIT)
airport.drive: 45 min by limousine bus, or about 30 min by high-speed boat

tip.r: Tipping is not part of Japanese culture and can even cause confusion; excellent service is already the standard and included in the price.

landmarks: Hells of Beppu (Jigoku Meguri)
Seven surreal geothermal springs, from cobalt-blue cauldrons to bubbling mud pots, form Japan's most famous circuit of steaming, otherworldly 'hells' for viewing rather than bathing.
Umi Jigoku (Sea Hell)
The most beautiful of Beppu's hells is a startlingly turquoise boiling pond wreathed in steam, set among landscaped gardens and lotus-filled greenhouse ponds.
Chinoike Jigoku (Blood Pond Hell)
Japan's oldest natural hell simmers a photogenic rust-red thanks to iron-rich clay, its crimson waters steaming dramatically against forested hills.
Takegawara Onsen
Beppu's grand 1879 bathhouse hides behind a sweeping Meiji-era wooden facade, famed for hot sand baths where attendants bury you in geothermally heated sand.
Kannawa District
Steam rises from every gutter in this atmospheric onsen village, where visitors cook eggs and vegetables in hell-steam kitchens between traditional inns.
Myoban Onsen
Thatched yunohana huts have harvested medicinal bath salts here for centuries, and milky-blue open-air baths overlook Beppu Bay from the sulfur-scented hillside.
Beppu Ropeway and Mount Tsurumi
A cable car glides up 1,375-meter Mount Tsurumi for sweeping panoramas of Beppu's steaming cityscape, especially magical with spring cherry blossoms or winter frost.
Beppu Tower
This retro 1957 lattice tower by Tokyo Tower's designer offers observation-deck views over the bay and the plumes of steam rising across the city.
Hyotan Onsen
The only onsen awarded three Michelin stars combines waterfall baths, sand baths and steam cuisine in a rambling, gourd-themed complex in Kannawa.
Takasakiyama Monkey Park
On a forested mountain between Beppu and Oita, over a thousand wild Japanese macaques roam freely around visitors at this beloved reserve founded in 1952.

train.note: Japan has no international trains, and no Shinkansen reaches Beppu. Beppu Station sits on JR Kyushu's Nippo Main Line, served by the tilting Sonic limited express to Hakata (Fukuoka) in about 2 hours, the Nichirin south to Miyazaki, and the Yufu / Yufuin-no-Mori scenic expresses inland to Yufuin. For Osaka or Tokyo you change at Hakata onto the San'yo and Tokaido Shinkansen, which is why many travellers prefer the overnight ferry or a flight from Oita Airport. Reserved seats on JR Kyushu expresses can be booked online in English about 1 month ahead.

bus.note: There are no international buses from Japan. Highway coaches use the stands at Beppu Station and the Kitahama stop in the centre: the Toyo no Kuni service run jointly by Nishitetsu (https://www.nishitetsu.jp/en/) and Oita Kotsu reaches Fukuoka's Tenjin in about 2 hours 40 minutes, and there are runs to Kumamoto, Nagasaki and Kagoshima plus overnight coaches to Osaka. Kamenoi Bus handles the local network up to the Beppu hells and Yufuin. Most seats can be reserved online or bought at the Kitahama counter.

intl.to: Osaka (Japan) - overnight sailing from Beppu Kokusai Kanko Port, about 10 min by bus from Beppu Station
Yawatahama, Shikoku (Japan) - sails from Beppu Kokusai Kanko Port

ferry.note: Beppu has no international sailings, but it is one of Kyushu's best ferry ports. MOL Sunflower's overnight ship leaves Beppu Kokusai Kanko Port in the evening and docks in Osaka the next morning, a 10-12 hour crossing with private cabins that doubles as a night's accommodation. Uwajima Unyu Ferry crosses the Bungo Channel to Yawatahama on Shikoku in under 3 hours, a useful shortcut if you are heading for Matsuyama. Cabins and vehicle space on the Osaka boat sell out in Golden Week and August, so book ahead.

half.name: Yufuin
half.blurb: A hot-spring resort town in a mountain valley with a lake reflecting Mount Yufu, known for boutique shops and quieter onsen than Beppu.

half.name: Usuki
half.blurb: A castle town on Kyushu's coast known for dozens of Buddhist images carved directly into stone cliff faces over 800 years ago.

full.name: Mount Aso
full.blurb: One of the world's largest active volcanic calderas, its crater accessible by cable car or road when volcanic activity permits.
